findings.title: A timer Pre-Vote round outlives the node's own leader establishment and demotes the new leader
findings.summary: With Pre-Vote enabled, the election timer runs pre_elect on a Candidate whose election is still in flight, leaving the real candidate untouched. When the original election then wins, establish_leader/become_leader do not clear pre_candidate. Late Pre-Vote grants pass RaftCore's leader-id correlation and handle_pre_vote_resp calls elect() on the established Leader without the timer's leader/voter checks. do_elect moves the vote to (term+1, self) while the Leader object of the previous term is kept, so the healthy leader steps down and try_leader_handler's leader.vote >= state.vote assertion panics RaftCore (debug builds); reproduced end-to-end (spec/confirmation-MC-1.md).

findings.title: Pre-Vote responses of an earlier round are counted by a later round with the same probe; after a membership change grant_by panics
findings.summary: A Pre-Vote round never changes the vote, so successive rounds at the same term probe the same leader id. RaftCore correlates PreVoteResponse notifications only by that leader id (does_pre_candidate_vote_match), contrary to its own comment that previous-round responses must be ignored. Operator rounds (trigger().elect(true)) have no rate limit, so a delayed grant of round A advances round B. If the membership changed between the rounds and removed the responder, Candidate::grant_by's expect panics and the RaftCore dies; reproduced end-to-end (spec/confirmation-MC-2.md).
